final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor offered no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the characterization of the same record. That clarification is valid as interpretation, but it does not satisfy the missing compliance predicates. The admissible evidence still shows: aggregate readiness clears by 2.4 points and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents; rollout begins at 3% with rollback capability; the affected health-plan benefits support segment remains below target and is not excluded from the random-tenant rollout; the risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not address that exposure; and policy states rollout controls and monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable, while disclosure duties remain when the affected segment is exposed. Because the unresolved disclosure/exclusion/approved-risk-acceptance condition remains unmet on this record, certification for launch now is not evidentially supported. The Actor's reframing may justify describing some readiness evidence as real but incomplete; it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats because the caveat here is an unresolved policy predicate, not a mere qualification on otherwise-satisfied compliance.
remaining_concerns: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by tenant and does not exclude the affected use case, so rollout controls do not satisfy the policy predicate.
The risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not mention the exposed health-plan benefits support segment, so there is no approved risk acceptance covering the known weakness.
No admissible evidence shows that the required pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case has been completed.

Public monitoring and model-card guidance support governance posture, but they do not override the internal requirement for exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or completed required disclosure before launch.
